Basic terminology and principles #1

Choosing the equipment #2

  • • according to:
  • – clinical status of a patient

  • • transducer = probe
  • convex - linear - endocavitary
  • • frequency 2 ,5 -3,5 - 5 - 7 - 10 - 12 MHz

Advantages of US #3

  • examination
  • • Harmless
  • • Available
  • • Compact
  • • Dynamic
  • • Good native contrast
  • • Good resolution with high frequency

Leading applications #4

  • • OB/GYN
  • • Pediatrics
  • • Gallbladder/bile duct pathology
  • • Liver difuse diseases
  • • Screening for HCC
  • • Small parts
  • • Cardiac (dynamics)
  • • ER/ICU/Point of care

Limits on US examination #5

  • • Attenuation / obesity
  • • uncooperative patients
  • • the lack of “acoustic window ”
  • – surgical bandages, patches
  • – interposition of air - bone – foreign bodies

US Image #6

  • Composed of a variety of bright
  • dots on a view that vary in
  • intensity, according to the
  • strength of returning echoes
  • from internal tissues/structures.
  • Provides anatomic and non-
  • anatomic information
  • “strong” returning echoes = bright dots
